top_comments.author: @SmethwickCouncilmanBint
top_comments.text: I work at a factory physically unboxing parts, screwing them together, then shipping them out. Got an email telling me to start using AI to be more productive. The AI can't unbox parts, screw them together, or ship them out. I have no idea what is being asked of me anymore. Pushing AI where it is literally useless and expecting results is negative productivity. Feels like "please use AI to pour two cups of water out of a 1 cup container of water." This is stupid.

I think for now, its very early to say anything, whether AI is bad or not. Imo, I think its very good. Using Claude and other ai programs has helped me fail faster, to realise what im good at and not good at. I'm able to move onto the next or solve a different problem just as quick compared to spending days weeks trying to understand what wouldnt have worked for me in the first place. 

People are naturally scared of new things because everyone is trying to complicate it too much allowing it to fully take over without thinking "hey how do I best utilise this for my life." Im sure when the whole internet boom came around people were scared af. Now its just everyday life.

top_comments.author: @LukRandom
top_comments.text:
Nah, I disagree. Did people stop drawewhen photography got invented? 

Did building a canal become less of an achievement when people stopped doing it by hand?

AI has not just made my work (as a software developer) much more productive and pleasant - no need to focus on minutia, but I get to work on the bigger picture. Also tweaking the AI is a sort of "natural language programming" and is interesting in its own right.

Even in my home IT it makes me do stuff that would take me a week of tinkering in a day.

And still there are huge areas that AI is absolutely crap. I tried to use it for creative writing and I gave up. It was all garbage.

I tried to use it for electronics design and 3d CAD, also horrible.

I tried to use it for video editing from my own clips to final result without having to touch it, just giving it a description of what I want the result to be... It was extremely limited. If your video contained people and such, yes, fine, but if it's on a technical topic forget it.

AI is a very niche thing now that they try to shove into everybody's throat. The funniest is at work where every senior dev has been telling the management "you've got this thing wrong, it is not capable of replacing even the most junior dev, but it's an amazing tool when used by a person with ability to use it". Still they push useless crap that costs millions...

I sometimes feel like in this true story about ancient Romans inventing the steam engine and they applied it to... A toy. They had no other use for it. Why would you want a machine to do physical work? What are all the slaves gonna do then? 😂

It feels like we are the Romans and the AI is the steam engine. Instead of using it for useful stuff we made a toy out of it.
